summary: full art and audio: every enemy and the boss through the M4 art chain, the environment kit and set dressing with section light, every sound effect from ElevenLabs, the bike chain and the floor glint, per-swatch damage marks and the near upper arm; done when no placeholder assets remain
read_first: docs/milestones/M6-plan.md §1 (the decisions D1-D29) and §5 (the done-when, row by row)
docs/milestones/M6-calls/<KEY>.md for the packages your lens covers (each logs its calls, ratchets and departures)

lenses.brief: The characters, judged from first-person stills against the picked concepts (assets/source/concepts/m6/kicker_c.jpg, thug_b.jpg, bruiser_a.jpg, boss_c.jpg; the Punk's and veteran's M4/M6 looks). Use docs/milestones/M6-codemap/art-chain.md §9's rubric per character (R1-R13; R1-R5 and R8 are critical), plus the M6 rows: the height read (the Bruiser at 2.05 m and Ox Pellerin at 2.3 m are scaled uniformly; do they read as bigger, not just scaled), the boss's budget, and the veteran against the base Punk (clearly different at 5 m, same silhouette). Also D6 (blood per swatch: a cap, a beanie, a strap, steel or the champion's belt scuffs but never bleeds; skin bleeds) and D7 (the near upper arm in the haymaker and the uppercut: ARM's A/B stills are in the common note; Game-boy is asked whether to keep it). Sources in captures_dir: r_punk, r_kicker, r_thug, r_bruiser, r_boss, r_dummy (each 'Look: <label> at 1 m', the view 8 degrees up then 6 down, with readability.json), lineup, heavies (2.5, 5 and 10 m beside a Punk), limbs (the player's own limbs). Strikes, flinches and damage looks are not in those acts: record what you need with tools/capture_bot.sh (crowd bot) or tools/capture_combos.sh into a folder of your own under captures/m6-final-chars/, at most 4 recordings. Cite each finding with its file and frame.

Accepted and not findings: the music loop is the one allowed placeholder (D25); the sounds are judged by Game-boy in the audition room, not by you; the game underneath is M5's (colliders, AI, numbers) and is held by test_m6_colliders.gd. Severity: high = it would spoil Game-boy's sign-off play or breaks the done-when (a placeholder left, a broken look at 1 m, a crash, a doorway or drop that no longer reads, a ledger over policy); medium = he'd notice it and it's wrong against the plan or the picked concept; low = polish. Give each finding the files to change, so the lead can partition the fixes.
